intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that otofaciocervical syndrome-1 (OTFCS1) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the EYA1 gene (601653) on chromosome 8q13.

checks.claim: Otofaciocervical syndrome-1 (OTFCS1) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the EYA1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: One patient with OFC syndrome carried a large deletion of the EYA1 gene region, confirming that OFC syndrome is allelic with BOR syndrome.
checks.explanation: The paper reports a large deletion of the EYA1 gene region (a contiguous gene deletion), not a heterozygous point mutation, in a single patient. The abstract does not state zygosity.

checks.claim: The EYA1 gene is located on chromosome 8q13.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutations in the EYA1 gene (localised to 8q13.3)
checks.explanation: 8q13.3 is within 8q13.

paragraphs.text: Otofaciocervical syndrome is a developmental disorder. Its main features are facial dysmorphism, abnormally shaped and low-set external ears, preauricular pits or fistulas, hearing loss, branchial cysts or fistulas, and abnormalities of the neck and shoulder girdle. These include a long neck, sloping shoulders and winged scapulae. Mild intellectual disability and short stature have been reported in some patients. The disorder overlaps with branchiootorenal (BOR) syndrome, which is also caused by mutation in EYA1, but renal anomalies are usually absent.

checks.claim: Otofaciocervical syndrome is a developmental disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: The distinction between BOR and other dysplasias, such as oto-facio-cervical syndrome (OFC)
checks.explanation: OFC described as a dysplasia; 'developmental disorder' implied rather than stated.

checks.claim: Facial dysmorphism is a main feature of otofaciocervical syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: autosomal recessively inherited disorder characterized by facial dysmorphism
checks.explanation: Facial dysmorphism is listed as a defining feature.

checks.claim: Abnormally shaped and low-set external ears are a main feature of otofaciocervical syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: external ear anomalies with preauricular pits and hearing impairment
checks.explanation: The abstract mentions external ear anomalies but does not say the ears are abnormally shaped or low-set.

checks.claim: Preauricular pits or fistulas are a main feature of otofaciocervical syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: external ear anomalies with preauricular pits and hearing impairment
checks.explanation: Preauricular pits are listed. Preauricular fistulas are not mentioned, but the claim says 'pits or fistulas'.

checks.claim: Hearing loss is a main feature of otofaciocervical syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: external ear anomalies with preauricular pits and hearing impairment
checks.explanation: Hearing impairment is listed as a feature.

checks.claim: Branchial cysts or fistulas are a main feature of otofaciocervical syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: branchial cysts or fistulas
checks.explanation: Branchial cysts or fistulas are listed as a feature.

checks.claim: Abnormalities of the neck and shoulder girdle are a main feature of otofaciocervical syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: long neck, sloping shoulders and clavicles, winged, low, and laterally set scapulae
checks.explanation: Neck and shoulder girdle abnormalities are described.

checks.claim: The neck and shoulder girdle abnormalities of otofaciocervical syndrome include a long neck.
checks.evidence_quote: long neck, sloping shoulders and clavicles
checks.explanation: The patient had a long neck.

checks.claim: The neck and shoulder girdle abnormalities of otofaciocervical syndrome include sloping shoulders.
checks.evidence_quote: long neck, sloping shoulders and clavicles
checks.explanation: The patient had sloping shoulders.

checks.claim: The neck and shoulder girdle abnormalities of otofaciocervical syndrome include winged scapulae.
checks.evidence_quote: winged, low, and laterally set scapulae
checks.explanation: The patient had winged scapulae.

checks.claim: Mild intellectual disability has been reported in some patients with otofaciocervical syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: anomalies of the vertebrae and the shoulder girdle, and mild intellectual disability
checks.explanation: Mild intellectual disability is listed as a feature.

checks.claim: Short stature has been reported in some patients with otofaciocervical syndrome.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 5 cited papers. The abstract does not mention short stature.

checks.claim: Otofaciocervical syndrome overlaps with branchiootorenal (BOR) syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: Oto-facio-cervical (OFC) syndrome is clinically similar to BOR syndrome, with clinical features in addition to those of BOR syndrome.

checks.claim: Branchiootorenal syndrome is also caused by mutation in EYA1.
checks.evidence_quote: Mutations in the EYA1 gene (localised to 8q13.3) account for nearly 70% of BOR syndrome cases exhibiting at least three of the major features.

checks.claim: Renal anomalies are usually absent in otofaciocervical syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: The absence of preauricular tags, lacrimal duct stenosis, and renal malformations
checks.explanation: Renal malformations were absent in this single patient. The abstract makes no general statement that they are usually absent.

paragraphs.text: Fara et al. (1967) described a Czech family with a dominantly inherited syndrome that they called dystrophia otofaciocervicalis. Affected members had facial dysmorphism, protruding and low-set ears, preauricular fistulas, hearing loss, a long neck, sloping shoulders and other shoulder-girdle anomalies.

checks.claim: Fara et al. (1967) described a Czech family with a dominantly inherited syndrome that they called dystrophia otofaciocervicalis.
checks.evidence_quote: [Familial oto-facio-cervical dysmorphia].
checks.explanation: The title says the condition is familial and gives a similar name ('dysmorphia', not 'dystrophia'). It does not say the family is Czech or that inheritance is dominant. Only the title was supplied.

checks.claim: Affected members of the Czech family described by Fara et al. (1967) had facial dysmorphism.
checks.evidence_quote: [Familial oto-facio-cervical dysmorphia].
checks.explanation: The title suggests facial malformation in this family, but no clinical details were supplied.

checks.claim: Affected members of the Czech family described by Fara et al. (1967) had protruding and low-set ears.
checks.explanation: Protruding or low-set ears are not in the title. Only the title was supplied.

checks.claim: Affected members of the Czech family described by Fara et al. (1967) had preauricular fistulas.
checks.explanation: Preauricular fistulas are not in the title. Only the title was supplied.

checks.claim: Affected members of the Czech family described by Fara et al. (1967) had hearing loss.
checks.explanation: Hearing loss is not in the title. Only the title was supplied.

checks.claim: Affected members of the Czech family described by Fara et al. (1967) had a long neck.
checks.explanation: A long neck is not specified in the title. Only the title was supplied.

checks.claim: Affected members of the Czech family described by Fara et al. (1967) had sloping shoulders.
checks.explanation: Sloping shoulders are not in the title. Only the title was supplied.

checks.claim: Affected members of the Czech family described by Fara et al. (1967) had other shoulder-girdle anomalies.
checks.explanation: Shoulder-girdle anomalies are not in the title. Only the title was supplied.

paragraphs.text: Dallapiccola and Mingarelli (1995) reported a sporadic patient with otofaciocervical syndrome. They argued that the disorder should be distinguished from branchiootorenal syndrome.

checks.claim: Dallapiccola and Mingarelli (1995) reported a sporadic patient with otofaciocervical syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: A sporadic patient with OFC syndrome is described.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

checks.claim: Dallapiccola and Mingarelli (1995) argued that otofaciocervical syndrome should be distinguished from branchiootorenal syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: support OFC syndrome being a unique, clinically recognisable entity
checks.explanation: The title and abstract argue for splitting OFC syndrome from BOR syndrome.

paragraphs.text: The family reported by Fara et al. (1967) showed autosomal dominant transmission of otofaciocervical syndrome.

checks.claim: The family with otofaciocervical syndrome reported by Fara et al. (1967) showed autosomal dominant transmission.
checks.explanation: The title says only 'familial'. It does not give the mode of inheritance (autosomal dominant). Only the title was supplied.

paragraphs.text: Otofaciocervical syndrome-2 (OTFCS2), an autosomal recessive form that includes immunodeficiency, is caused by mutation in the PAX1 gene.

checks.claim: Otofaciocervical syndrome-2 (OTFCS2) is an autosomal recessive form of otofaciocervical syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: A hypofunctional PAX1 mutation causes autosomal recessively inherited otofaciocervical syndrome.
checks.explanation: The paper describes autosomal recessive OFCS caused by PAX1, but it does not use the 'OTFCS2' label or present it as a distinct form.

checks.claim: Otofaciocervical syndrome-2 (OTFCS2) includes immunodeficiency.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not mention immunodeficiency.

checks.claim: Otofaciocervical syndrome-2 (OTFCS2) is caused by mutation in the PAX1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: establish PAX1 as a new disease-causing gene for OFCS
checks.explanation: A homozygous PAX1 c.497G>T (p.G166V) mutation was found to cause the PAX1-related form of OFCS.

paragraphs.text: Rickard et al. (2001) found a heterozygous deletion involving the EYA1 gene on chromosome 8q in a patient with otofaciocervical syndrome. They concluded that OTFCS is a contiguous gene deletion syndrome that is allelic to BOR syndrome. Their analysis also narrowed the critical region for Duane syndrome.

checks.claim: Rickard et al. (2001) found a heterozygous deletion involving the EYA1 gene on chromosome 8q in a patient with otofaciocervical syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: One patient with OFC syndrome carried a large deletion of the EYA1 gene region, confirming that OFC syndrome is allelic with BOR syndrome.
checks.explanation: A deletion in an OFC patient is reported, and EYA1 is placed at 8q13.3. The abstract does not explicitly state that the deletion is heterozygous; it says the deletions were de novo.

checks.claim: Rickard et al. (2001) concluded that otofaciocervical syndrome is a contiguous gene deletion syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: Oto-facio-cervical (OFC) syndrome is a contiguous gene deletion syndrome involving EYA1
checks.explanation: This is stated in the title.

checks.claim: Rickard et al. (2001) concluded that otofaciocervical syndrome is allelic to branchiootorenal syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: confirming that OFC syndrome is allelic with BOR syndrome

checks.claim: The analysis by Rickard et al. (2001) narrowed the critical region for Duane syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: reduces the critical region for Duane syndrome (an eye movement disorder) to between markers D8S553 and D8S1797, a genetic distance of approximately 1 cM

paragraphs.text: Estefania et al. (2006) identified a heterozygous splice site mutation in the EYA1 gene in a patient with otofaciocervical syndrome. This showed that a point mutation in EYA1, and not only a contiguous gene deletion, can cause the phenotype.

checks.claim: Estefania et al. (2006) identified a heterozygous splice site mutation in the EYA1 gene in a patient with otofaciocervical syndrome.
checks.evidence_quote: we show here that an OFC patient bears a single-nucleotide substitution in a splice site of EYA1
checks.explanation: Splice site mutation in one OFC patient supported; heterozygosity not stated in abstract.

checks.claim: The finding by Estefania et al. (2006) showed that a point mutation in EYA1, not only a contiguous gene deletion, can cause the otofaciocervical syndrome phenotype.
checks.evidence_quote: Our results indicate that not only major rearrangements, but also point mutations altering the EYA1 reading frame, can be found in patients with OFC syndrome.
checks.explanation: Matches the conclusion, contrasting with contiguous deletion hypothesis.
